original.title: Sequential inference as a mode of cognition and its correlates in fronto-parietal and hippocampal brain regions

correction_effects: Original joint window recursion C3 repeatedly used already-smoothed boundary p(x_(t-n)|o_(1:t-1)) and double-counted earlier information; suboptimal in original first-order HMM.
Corrected optimal sequential recursion C5 instead uses p(x_(t-n)|o_(1:t-n)) separately computed by filtering at sequence boundary.

Under corrected C5, marginal belief in present x_t and current-state task choice in original first-order HMM task equal Bayesian filtering C1; optimal sequential versus filter not behaviorally identifiable.
All original fitted likelihoods and actual VBM numerical analyses remain as reported; normative interpretation and specific source-level causal strategy identification do not.
Eleven of 79 source L=1 subjects can implement optimal sequential rather than filtering; ΔLL is ambiguous between suboptimal vs optimal and sequential-vs-filter contrasts.
NEVER qualify superseded claim of equally optimal but behaviorally distinct sequential strategy.
